about: Polymer crystal unit cells from their original crystal-structure papers (one entry per paper and form): the paper's cell and heavy atoms, hydrogens from the paper or placed geometrically (tools/make_polymer_crystals.py), written in P1. PTFE's paper gives lattices and helix symmetry only: its chains are generated from the helix and the cited lattice, not refined (see each entry's helix block). These are DFT unit cells (VASP relaxation, phono3py); large MD cells are built from them.

crystals.name: Polyethylene, orthorhombic
crystals.source: C. W. Bunn, Trans. Faraday Soc. 35, 482 (1939)
crystals.where: cell and space group p. 483; carbon positions p. 490 (x = 0.038 a, y = 0.065 b; 0.038, .935, .250 ...)
crystals.density_note: the paper gives no density; 4 CH2 in the paper's cell give 1.008 g/cm3
crystals.use: PE crystal: VASP and phono3py thermal conductivity; the crystalline layers of semicrystalline PE

crystals.name: Polyethylene, monoclinic
crystals.source: K. Seto, T. Hara & K. Tanaka, Jpn. J. Appl. Phys. 7, 31 (1968)
crystals.where: cell, space group and density p. 32; phi = 90 deg p. 34; no coordinate table in the paper
crystals.space_group: C2/m (b unique, b the chain axis)
corrections: the paper prints no atomic coordinates: C placed from its chain setting (zigzag plane perpendicular to a, phi = 90 deg, p. 34) with the orthorhombic chain geometry it assumes (Bunn 1939: C-C 1.53 A)
crystals.use: PE crystal polymorph (strained or drawn PE)

crystals.name: Isotactic polypropylene, α (α2, ordered)
crystals.source: M. Hikosaka & T. Seto, Polym. J. 5, 111 (1973)
crystals.where: cells p. 112 (specimen B: a 6.65, b 20.73, c 6.50 A, beta 98 deg 40 min); Table Ia p. 115 (carbon only)
crystals.space_group: P21/c (b unique, c the chain axis)
crystals.density_note: the paper gives no density; 12 C3H6 in the specimen B cell give 0.947 g/cm3
corrections: the appendix's equivalent positions (pp. 126-127) do not fit Table Ia; the standard P21/c positions (x,y,z; -x,1/2+y,1/2-z; -x,-y,-z; x,1/2-y,1/2+z) do: every C-C 1.54 A and the paper's structure factors of Table Ib are reproduced
the ordered limiting structure alpha2 (all chains up/down as in P21/c); the alpha1 form is the statistical C2/c up/down model of the same coordinates

crystals.name: Poly(ethylene oxide), monoclinic
crystals.where: cell and space group p. 672; Table II p. 674 (all atoms, hydrogens included)
crystals.space_group: P21/a (b unique, c the chain axis)
crystals.density_note: the paper gives no density; 28 C2H4O in the paper's cell give 1.229 g/cm3

crystals.name: Poly(vinylidene fluoride), β (form I)
crystals.source: R. Hasegawa, Y. Takahashi, Y. Chatani & H. Tadokoro, Polym. J. 3, 600 (1972)
crystals.where: cell p. 601; Table I(a) p. 603 (planar zigzag model, hydrogens included); density p. 604
corrections: F y/b = 0.335 instead of the printed 0.355 (Table I(a)): 0.355 gives C-F 1.40 A and F-C-F 101 deg against the paper's stated C-F 1.34 A and F-C-F 108 deg (p. 603), which give 0.335; the printed form III value (0.330) and the disordered model's F pair (mean 0.332) agree with 0.335
the ordered planar zigzag model (a), not the statistical +-7 deg model (b)

crystals.name: Poly(vinylidene fluoride), α (form II)
crystals.source: R. Hasegawa, Y. Takahashi, Y. Chatani & H. Tadokoro, Polym. J. 3, 600 (1972)
crystals.where: cell and density p. 604; Table III p. 605 (hydrogens included)
crystals.space_group: P21/c (b unique, c the chain axis)
crystals.use: PVDF crystal (TGTG', the common melt-crystallised form)

crystals.name: Polyoxymethylene, orthorhombic
crystals.source: G. Carazzolo & M. Mammi, J. Polym. Sci. A 1, 965 (1963)
crystals.where: cell and density p. 968; space group p. 969; Table I p. 974 (C and O)
corrections: this paper's structure is the orthorhombic (2/1 helix) form; it gives no coordinates for the common trigonal 9/5 helix form

crystals.name: Nylon 6, α
crystals.source: D. R. Holmes, C. W. Bunn & D. J. Smith, J. Polym. Sci. 17, 159 (1955)
crystals.where: cell, space group and density p. 161; Table II p. 172 (heavy atoms)
crystals.space_group: P21 (b unique, b the chain axis)
corrections: molecule A's O z = -0.027 instead of the printed -0.007 (C=O 1.15 A as printed): molecule B prints -0.027, and molecule C, which the paper says is A displaced by 3/14 b and c/2 (p. 163), prints 0.473 = 0.5 - 0.027
molecules B and D: the CH2 zigzag phase swapped (x 0.544 <-> 0.460, z +-0.007 <-> -+0.007) so it fits their own N, C and O (as printed N-CH2 is 1.26 A and C(O)-CH2 1.19 A; swapped 1.48 and 1.44 A)

crystals.name: Nylon 66, α
crystals.source: C. W. Bunn & E. V. Garner, Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 189, 39 (1947)
crystals.where: cell p. 39 and p. 49; density p. 42; coordinates p. 49 (heavy atoms)

crystals.name: Poly(ethylene terephthalate), triclinic
crystals.source: R. de P. Daubeny, C. W. Bunn & C. J. Brown, Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 226, 531 (1954)
crystals.where: cell p. 531 and p. 533; density p. 536; Table 1 p. 538 (heavy atoms)

crystals.name: Poly(L-lactide), α
crystals.where: cell, space group and density p. 8388; Table 1 p. 8389 (heavy atoms and the methine H)

crystals.name: Natural rubber (cis-1,4-polyisoprene)
crystals.where: cell p. 4860 and Fig. 5 p. 4862 (beta 93.1 deg; the abstract prints 94.6); Table 2 p. 4862 (all atoms)
crystals.space_group: P21/a (b unique, c the chain axis)
crystals.density_note: the paper gives no density; 8 C5H8 in the paper's cell give 1.007 g/cm3
corrections: beta = 93.1 deg (text and Fig. 5) rather than the abstract's 94.6 deg: the coordinates give regular bond lengths with 93.1 deg only

ordered model: every site holds the Table 2 molecule. The paper refines a statistical structure in which the mirror image about y = 1/8 occupies a site with 33 % weight; a DFT cell needs one orientation

crystals.name: Polytetrafluoroethylene, phase IV (15/7 helix)
crystals.source: E. S. Clark & L. T. Muus, Z. Kristallogr. 117, 119 (1962)
crystals.where: hexagonal cell (25 C) p. 121; 15/7 helix packed in P31, one chain per cell, p. 127; no atomic coordinates in the paper
crystals.density_note: the paper gives no density; 15 CF2 in the paper's hexagonal cell give 2.302 g/cm3
crystals.coordinates: generated from the helix symmetry and the cited lattice (tools/make_polymer_crystals.py), not refined

helix.bonds_from: Hasegawa, Takahashi, Chatani & Tadokoro, Polym. J. 3, 600 (1972), p. 603

corrections: no atomic coordinates in the paper: the chain is generated from the 15/7 helix and the cited lattice, not refined: 15 CF2 in 7 turns span c exactly (rise 1.3000 A, twist 168.00 deg per CF2), C-C 1.54 A, C-F 1.34 A, F-C-F 108 deg (Hasegawa, Takahashi, Chatani & Tadokoro, Polym. J. 3, 600 (1972), p. 603); this gives C-C-C 115.56 deg, carbon helix radius 0.415 A and fluorine radius 1.618 A (Bunn & Howells, Nature 174, 549 (1954): 116 deg, about 0.42 A and 1.64 +- 0.05 A); one chain on the cell axis, setting angle 6 deg (the paper gives none: the one with the longest shortest F...F between chains, 2.802 A)
at this setting angle the chain's own twofold axes fall on the lattice's, so the cell also has them: P3112 (No. 151, origin at z = 11/30), which contains the paper's P31
crystals.use: PTFE crystal between 19 and 30 C (room temperature), the form most used in simulations; VASP and phono3py

crystals.name: Polytetrafluoroethylene, phase II (13/6 helix)
crystals.source: E. S. Clark & L. T. Muus, Z. Kristallogr. 117, 119 (1962)
crystals.where: oblique (probably triclinic) cell at 0 C, a' = b' = 5.59 A, c = 16.88 A, gamma = 119.3 deg, p. 121; 13/6 helix on that lattice pp. 123 and 126; no atomic coordinates in the paper
crystals.density_note: the paper gives no density; 13 CF2 in the paper's oblique cell give 2.347 g/cm3
crystals.coordinates: generated from the helix symmetry and the cited lattice (tools/make_polymer_crystals.py), not refined

helix.bonds_from: Hasegawa, Takahashi, Chatani & Tadokoro, Polym. J. 3, 600 (1972), p. 603

corrections: the paper treats the lattice as the periodic arrangement of the chain axes (p. 121) and gives no space group: one chain per cell, written as P1 with alpha = beta = 90 deg (c along the chain axis)

no atomic coordinates in the paper: the chain is generated from the 13/6 helix and the cited lattice, not refined: 13 CF2 in 6 turns span c exactly (rise 1.2985 A, twist 166.15 deg per CF2), C-C 1.54 A, C-F 1.34 A, F-C-F 108 deg (Hasegawa, Takahashi, Chatani & Tadokoro, Polym. J. 3, 600 (1972), p. 603); this gives C-C-C 115.48 deg, carbon helix radius 0.417 A and fluorine radius 1.619 A (Bunn & Howells, Nature 174, 549 (1954): 116 deg, about 0.42 A and 1.64 +- 0.05 A); one chain on the cell axis, setting angle 25 deg (the paper gives none: the one with the longest shortest F...F between chains, 2.723 A)
